description: H4A-FIX2 — narrow, per-file registry of DEEP_MAIN synthetic residue that is INTENTIONAL_TERMINAL_RESIDUE, not a cleanup defect: the fixture creates a row a named, verified product invariant then forbids deleting. Each entry's table/invariant was individually confirmed by attempting a raw superuser DELETE against a real leftover row from that file's own fixture (see docs/architecture/assurance-tiers.md's DEEP_MAIN section) — never assumed from a table name alone. maxSchools bounds how many synthetic schools that file may leave behind (set with modest headroom above one observed run, not exact-counted every subtest — tighten with a second observed run before relying on it to catch a 1-row regression); anything above it is an unexpected leak, not covered residue. This manifest never uses a table-only or SYNTHETIC_*-wildcard entry (see scripts/validate-intentional-residue.mjs, which enforces that).

knownCleanupDefectNotResidue.note: lib/quiz/quizDelivery.integration.test.ts is NOT intentional residue — its blocker is ingestion_runs rows still present after the file's own cleanup already deletes ingestion_runs scoped by initiated_by. Root cause is very likely a fire-and-forget/async write racing past the after() hook (the codebase documents this exact pattern elsewhere as 'fire-and-forget contract'), not a product immutability rule. This is a genuine CLEANUP_DEFECT, left open for a future phase, not registered here.
